answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a ivory as the anchor of the cost. A ember stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a marble...
